360.fullDescription: This starts on DNR land about 5.5 miles up Palo Alto Rd.  Get some views at beginning of hike looking south up the Dungeness.  Recent logging activity.   https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/map-0e4f5cc-12 Pros Other
360.pros: Wed. hike.  Views looking south up the Dungeness.  PT-J-1800 Rd.  Enters USFS land in about a mile (?)
360.others: Hunting in Fall, so be careful!  Could be some logging activity.

anderson.fullDescription: Head to the Tamanowas Rock Sanctuary (Sacred Rock) via Split Rock from the Savage Memorial Trail, Cascade Trail, and San Juan Trail, on the west side of the lake.  Many possible loops in this state park.  https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/map-1340351-11 Pros Other
anderson.pros: Sacred, interesting rocks.  The other one off of the Cascade Trail is called:  Peregrine Rock, the largest erratic rock in Jefferson County?
anderson.others: Usually a Wed. hike.  Slot rock is the 1st trail past the Priv. Property sign.  Can combine with the DNR S. trails and get 9.6 mi. and 1,530'  (~ 4.5 mi. on south & 829')

anderson-lake.fullDescription: This DNR area at Anderson Lake State Park is a multi-use area for bikes, horses, and hikers--not used much by hikers.  There are some ramps and fun jumps to see that the bikers use; but hikers can usually walk around.  There used to be slight viewpoints; but those are getting overgrown by trees.  Look for bowling pin on one trail!  Ferns and mushrooms are fun! Pros Other
anderson-lake.pros: Not busy at all by dog walkers and hikers and seldom see bikers on week days.  When combine both and do other side as well, you can get up to 9.6 miles and 1,530'

anderson-lake-state.fullDescription: We start at Anderson Lake State Park and travel to the ODT via the Olympic Trail. This new trail segment is 3.15 miles long and goes to Milo Curry Road in a out-and-back. Pros Other

aurora.fullDescription: This is an obscure trail leaving from 101 on edge of Lake Crescent.  It is a relentless trail (1,150'/mi.) climbing ~ 3,500' in 3 miles up to Aurora Ridge.  One can stop and turn-around there after about 3.4 mi. or go right on the Aurora Ridge Trail another 2.5 miles to Sourdough Mt. where there used to be an old shelter.  One may get glimpses of Mt. Olympus to the south. Pros Other
aurora.pros: Will most likely not see any one!
aurora.others: Trail not marked and hard to find.  Off of Maple Point between M.P. 225 & 226 near turn-out sign.

aurora-ridge.fullDescription: This is a relatively quieter hike in ONP ~ 2.5 mi. up the Sol Duc Rd.!  It follows and old roadbed for almost a mile amongst tall alders and then proceeds switchbacks through this 2nd-growth forest.  Reach the ridge-crest and follow the rounded crest of Aurora Ridge to a junction at about 5.5 miles, which leads to Eagle Lakes and the source of Eagle Creek that drains into Lake Crescent. One can turn-around here or continue down to the largest Eagle Lake for about .6 mi. Pros Other
aurora-ridge.pros: Not a busy hike.  May find salmon berries in the Fall.

badger.fullDescription: This is a shorter loop into Badger Valley but does not include the lakes.  Go into Badger Valley for about a mile; then turn and go uphill towards Elk Mt. on a more primitive and sometimes steep trail for ~ 1.5 miles.  Can climb up to top of Elk Mt. @ 6,782', which adds another couple hundred feet.  Nice views! Pros Other

badger-valley.fullDescription: This is a difficult, brutally descending hike down to Grand Lake & going on to Moose Lake before an equally grueling, exposed ascent. Bring plenty of water. Experienced mt. road drivers needed for the drive to the end of Obstruction Point Road.  It's nice to do a loop whether clockwise or counter-clockwise. Pros Other
badger-valley.others: Grueling descent and gain.  It is advised to make it an early start by about an hour, as it's a long day!  The drive out there takes about 1-1/2 hours from Sequim, etc.

barnes.fullDescription: Pass turn-off to Marymere Falls @ about 3/4 mi. & proceed up the valley along Barnes Creek, crossing 3 bridges and some old-growth, giant trees. At ~ 3.75 miles, pass Dismal Draw Camp and proceed on up to the Aurora Divide junction at ~4-1/2 miles and @ 2,050', which is a good turn-around point.  Views of Mt. Storm King. Pros Other
barnes.others: Slippery bridges--1st one w/o handrail @ ~ 1.4 mi.  Two-three slides which could present a problem. 3,300 cumulative?

blue.fullDescription: This is a nature trail to the top of Blue Mt. near the Deer Park Campground.  Offers great views of the Olympics, Cascades, Vancouver Island, the Strait of Juan de Fuca, the Gray Wolf area, etc.  Blue Mt. gets its name due to it geographic location in the large rain shadow cast by Mt. Olympus and the Bailey Range. Pros Other

blyn.fullDescription: Hike up ~ 3-1/2 miles to the Blyn Cell Towers off of Casselary Rd.  This is a multi-use DNR area.  Get views into the Olympics and may even see Mt. Rainier!  May add on a section for views from above the Layton Hills Horse Camp area, or do an adventure route through the woods on the return!  Be flexible!   Can take the group to the Historic Larrance Farm, a part of the Jefferson Land Trust for the viewing of the salmon at Salmon Creek, a Fish & Wildlife site before or after this hike, since they are both in the same area off Uncas Rd. in Discovery Bay. Pros Other
blyn.pros: Fish in late Sept./early Oct. (6th).  Was a little too late on Oct. 6th.  Can also see if we see salmon further up Salmon Creek from the Wally Bowman Bridge on Uncas Rd.
blyn.others: Try to go at time that a Sandy, who is a volunteer for the Fish & Wildlife Dept. is there (?)

blyn-tower.fullDescription: Hike up ~ 3-1/2 miles to the Blyn Cell Towers off of Uncas Rd.   Very difficult stream crossing possible.  This is a multi-use DNR area.  Get views into the Olympics and may even see Mt. Rainier! Pros Other
blyn-tower.others: 922 W. Uncas Road --private land--owner is greg

bogachiel.fullDescription: Gives a good flavor of a temperate rainforest & old-growth trees w/o going to the crowded Hoh!   Natl. Park is at  ~ 1.6 mi.  Can add on the Ira Spring Wetland Trail loop.  Can also see the site of an old Homestead while doing the Bogachiel Trail.   If proceed to the 6 mi. mark, you reach a junction of the Snider-Jackson Trail, site of the former Bogachiel Ranger Station; but this was washed away in 1989.  Can go to ~ the 3-mile section to river and have lunch before deciding on afternoon route. Pros Other
bogachiel.pros: Not a busy hike but most pleasant.  Can turn-around before the slide section and rope area and have lunch at river bank or proceed on.  If proceed, need poles and H20 shoes.
bogachiel.others: Avoid in the Fall when there is bow hunting (starts 9/01 and elk hunting!  Watch for seasons! 2-hour drive.  If go beyond the slide up the ropes, it can get more difficult.

boulder.fullDescription: Hikers depart from Madison Falls along the old roadbed and bypass up to Glines Canyon Dam, which is ~ 3.75 miles.  The Smokey Bottom Trail departs just west of the dam along the shoreline and in the old Lake Mills lakebed.  Spring (late May) is a good time to see some native flowers that were planted during the Elwha Revegetation Project like lupine, Nootka roses, Oregon sunshine, etc. Pros Other
boulder.pros: We hit the lupine perfectly on 5/24/2024.   Not wilderness to campground
boulder.others: There may be some mud & wet area when crossing Upper Stukey Creek.  Use caution on crossing on log.  The Gray Wolf crew logged it out with ~ 74 trees in 3/2024 (Lisa/Neil)

boulder-shelter.fullDescription: This is a longer day hike. Start at the Upper Dungeness T.H.; cross Royal Creek, hike beyond Camp Handy, splitting off beyond and climbing steadily ~ 3 miles up to Boulder Shelter / Boulder Camp, which is below Marmot Pass.  Can get clear views westward into the Milk Creek and Heather Creek drainages. Pros Other
boulder-shelter.pros: 6/28/2024--Flowers were exquisite!  Marmot Pass trail right before small creek that you cross going to Boulder Shelter. Took ~ 7-1/2 hrs. Suggest Early Start? 1-hr. drive ea. way
boulder-shelter.others: Paul says to head past the Shelter a short bit on trail to Home Lake; and there is a good view.  Charlia Lakes trail goes to left at juncture ~ 1/4 mi. from Shelter.

borderline.fullDescription: This hike borders DNR land and Olympic Natl. Park land off of Deer Park Rd.  Do and out-and-back going to Marmot Loop off of Blue Mt. Rd. and return back to Deer Park Rd.  Headwaters of Bagley Creek with ~ 10 shallow stream crossings.  W. Hemlock stand. Pros Other
borderline.pros: ~ 7.6 mi. up Deer Park Rd. to yellow gate about .1 mi. back from parking pull-out on E. side before the gate going up to Deer Park.
borderline.others: Berries in Fall; watch for hunting season in mid-to-end of Oct., especially.  Can be muddy w/~ 10 shallow stream crossings!

buckhorn.fullDescription: Trail is Tubal Cain Trail #840 up the Dungeness.  From Copper Creek (see Tubal Cain write-up), climb steadily ~2.5 mi. along valley's west wall on switchbacks.  Beautiful, picturesque views of Buckhorn Mt. & Iron Mt. at the end of valley.  At ~5.8 mi. & a 1,000' climb, reach Buckhorn Lake junction.  Go down 100' in less than a 1/2 mi. to the tiny lake or climb up towards a view/high point @ Buckhorn an addtl. .8 mi. & another ~ 675'elev. but is not Buckhorn Pass nor Marmot. Pros Other
buckhorn.pros: Wonderful wildflowers if you hit it right.  July (?)/August?
buckhorn.others: Buckhorn Lake is ~12.4 mi. R.T./~ 2,100'.   Bev did another .8 up from Buckhorn Lake junct. and another ~ 672'.  They did the shortcut back, however; but she did not like it

buckhorn-pass.fullDescription: This is beyond Buckhorn Lake turn-off and heads up to the "Pass".  Fairly easy ~ 3.6 miles to Copper Creek.  Then, start climbing up towards Buckhorn Lake turn-off @ ~ 5.8 mi. and then on up to the plateau between Buckhorn and Marmot passes.  Wildflowers are often seen in the meadows heading up beyond Buckhorn Lake & quite beautiful.  There is a 3/4 mi. "shortcut" which cuts mileage down to 12 miles.  It's steeper & 1/3 mi. beyond Copper Creek @ 2nd switchback. Pros Other
buckhorn-pass.pros: Mileage depends upon if the shortcut is taken.  The shortcut does cut out about 2 miles.  It is steep & rocky in sections but quite doable.  Regular route is a more gentle grade.
buckhorn-pass.others: 3.2 mi. to juncture with Tull Canyon.  Another ~ .5 to Copper Creek.  2.2 mi. to Buckhorn Lake, if don't take shortcut. About another .8 mi. + to Buckhorn Pass & ~ 672'.

burnt.fullDescription: Starts at the parking area off of Johnson Creek and Easterly and will begin with a steep and continuous incline.   This hike will likely include the radio tower and at least one overlook…Weather and group dependent. Pros Other
burnt.pros: Many variations of routes and distances up here.  Johnson Creek to views Left is a Wed. hike.  Up to Radio tower is about 5.6 mi. & 1,200'.
burnt.others: Just don't do during the main hunting season of mid-Oct. to end of Oct. and late hunt of 4 days in mid-Nov.  Check the WDFW website for exact dates.  Also logging activity.

burnt-hill.fullDescription:
We will park up at the first gate @ Johnson Creek Road. (limited space) We will start up the road for a bit then take a side trail that winds through the woods to the cabin.  The trail has a bit of a steady incline some areas of mud and pools of water so wear waterproof boots and gators. 
There are some nice view points where you can see over Happy Valley, out to the straits and protection island. After the cabin we will head out towards the gravel pit area and back to the yellow gates.  If people would like to end now they can choose to go back to the car or continue on to the southeast overlook for views of Sequim Bay this will add another 2 miles to the hike total. Pros Other
burnt-hill.pros: Many variations of routes and distances up here.  Johnson Creek to views Left is a Wed. hike.  Up to Radio tower is about 5.6 mi. & 1,200'.
burnt-hill.others: Just don't do during the main hunting season of mid-Oct. to end of Oct. and late hunt of 4 days in mid-Nov.  Check the WDFW website for exact dates.  Also logging activity.

burnt-hill-from.fullDescription: See some different parts of Burnt Hill. Park at the Louella Cabin off Palo Alto Road. Hike up rutted and often muddy roads and trails to access the logging road system that rings Burnt Hill. Travelling in a rough figure 8 pattern, we will decide at 6.25 miles if we want to hike out to the NE overlook for a view toward Discovery Bay and Port Townsend, which will add 2 miles to the hike. We will then head back toward the Louella Cabin. Poles are recommended for the steep sections of this hike. There are some areas of mud and pools of water so wear waterproof boots and gaiters. Pros Other

camp.fullDescription: Camp Handy is on the Upper Dungeness River.  Park at the Upper Dungeness T.H. Parking lot.  Go ~ 1 mile on the trail, crossing Royal Creek on the left over an impressive bridge.  Trail parallels the river for the most part.  Enjoy old-growth Douglas fir and a green carpet of moss along this trail.  Camp Handy is an excellent destination for first-time backpackers, as it is fairly easy to get to. Pros Other
camp.pros: This could be a good Wed. hike.
camp.others: Hunting season in the fall between 9/15-9/25 (High Hunt) and in Oct., as this is a base for some hunters.  WILDERNESS LIMIT OF 12 AFTER CROSSING ROYAL CREEK.

cascade.fullDescription: Hike leaves the Madison Falls area and uses the Bypass Trail to get to the trailhead, which starts just less than a mile from Madison Falls.  Ascend high above the Elwha River Valley.  Will go through old-growth forest and some madronas.  Reach a ledge at ~ 900' & may get views over to Mt. Baldy.  Steadily climb and then get to a mossy basalt ledge at ~ 1,825' & the official trail end.   Limited views but a good workout! Pros Other
cascade.others: There is a 1/2 mile scramble to the very top for better views but do not recommend this.  This would be an "Ad Hoc" hike for the select few.  Use Caution!

cassidy.fullDescription: This is a road hike on DNR land off of Atterbury Rd. and is an out-and-back hike. Has a loop around Mcdonald Creek.  Has hair Ice if temps 30-32F. Pros Other
cassidy.pros: Great views couple of mi. up. It is ~5.5 mi. to road end.  Nice lunch spot at a landing as you start heading down.  ~1,200' elev. to road end. Varying distances/mileages given.
cassidy.others: Wed. hike would be a loop off of road, which is about 4.5 mi. and 400'.  This would be an Easy hike.  Avoid the Fall during hunting season

cassidy-creek.fullDescription: This is a road hike on DNR land off of Atterbury Rd. and is an out-and-back hike. At the first high point at ~ 2 miles, there are great views of Blue Mt., Tyler Peak, and other surrounding mountains in the Olympics.  This is a multi-use area with a variety of other routes and trails off of the main road.  Go to high point for more views and to road end to complete the route!  Can do a loop coming back through the woods, if feeling "adventurous"! Pros Other
cassidy-creek.pros: Great views couple of mi. up. It is ~5.5 mi. to road end.  Nice lunch spot at a landing as you start heading down.  ~1,200' elev. to road end. Varying distances/mileages given.
cassidy-creek.others: Wed. hike would be a loop off of road, which is about 4.5 mi. and 400'.  This would be an Easy hike.  Avoid the Fall during hunting season

cat.fullDescription: This is accessed off of Diamond Point Road and is an area on the eastern edge of Miller Peninsula.  This is a small lake. Pros Other
cat.pros: At one time we saw a pair of trumpeter swans here!
cat.others: Wed. hike.  Call (360) 460-2820 to get permission.

chetzemoka.fullDescription: This is a historical, interpretive trail in Port Townsend, which commemorates Chief Chetzemoka (Anglicized name for the Chief).  There are a total of 18 signs educating the public about the relationship between the S’Klallam people and the European settlers who arrived in the 1800’s.  Starts at Haines Place Park and Ride in PT. Pros Other
chetzemoka.pros: See the Camas in May in the Qatay Prairie?  Do earlier in May?  May have lunch at Aldrich's Grocery in Uptown Port Townsend.
chetzemoka.others: May need to pay a bus fare from the Haines Place P&R and Jefferson County Transit Station (Gateway Park) near Safeway; but it's usually free!

crown.fullDescription: Start from Crown Park in P.A. and walk down to beach area, which is a short, but very steep decline for ~ 100'.  Then, walk along the pleasant beach under towering cliffs, for about 4 miles.  One can proceed further, if allowed. Pros Other
crown.others: Tides (less than 4')  If warm, the sun reflects from the towering cliffs; and it can be quite warm!

dan.fullDescription: Hike on mt. bike trails and logging roads to this cell tower area, which overlooks the Elwha Valley to the South with spectacular views up into the Olympics and with Eden Valley to the north and views to Striped Peak and out to the Strait of Juan de Fuca and over to Vancouver Island. Pros Other
dan.others: Watch for hunting season and come in the back way maybe?  Some trails might be closed off to hikers and are biking trails!  Also, watch for any logging activity.

deadfall.fullDescription: This is another approach up to Mt. Zion not often used and is longer and steeper than the traditional route.  It is appropriately named for the somewhat steep grade of ~ 23%.  Gain 560' in first 1/2-3/4 mile before joining the Snow Creek Trail up to Mt. Zion.  Climb 1,680' in 1.8 miles with a total of 2,240' elev. gain.  Distance reflects whether one chooses to go to rock outcropping use caution) with views before the actual Mt. Zion summit (site of old lookout) w/ obstructed views. Pros Other
deadfall.others: Not as many rhodys, however.  Come from Lord's Lake area.  T.H. is harder to find, as the road is not well marked.  Before Bon Jon Pass.  Is near a "shooting gallery".

deer.fullDescription: Reverse hike leaving from Deer Park Campground.  Hike about .3 mile on the Deer Ridge Trail before descending down the 3-Forks Trail for ~ 4 miles and ~ 19 switchbacks to the confluence of 3 creeks/rivers:  Gray Wolf, Grand, and Cameron.  Beautiful views of Gray Wolf and Grand Ridges, and Grand Valley before soon entering the trees from the top.  Come to the 3-Forks Shelter and Camp.  Can continue an addtl. 1/2 mi. to Gray Wolf Camp and junction with the Gray Wolf Trail. Pros Other

deer-hair.fullDescription: Park near picnic area near Hurricane Hill Trail & hike on the paved trail to 5,757' gaining ~ 600'.  Backtrack from top down ~ .1 mi. to the Elwha Trail.  This trail drops down to what is called Deer Hair Rock or the Elwha Overlook @ ~ 4,643'.  This hike is a reverse hike where you drop ~ 800-1,000'+ to the overlook and then climb back out!  Has excellent views overlooking the Elwha River & Valley.  Wildflowers can be nice!  Couple of steep, scree sections, so poles are most helpful. Pros Other
deer-hair.pros: ~ 2 mi. to junction on Hurricane Hill from 3rd parking lot.  Gain ~ 600'+.  Almost 4 mi. to Deer Hair Rock. Descend ~ 964'/Took ~ 2 hours one way.  Total ~ 1,780'/7.75 mi.
deer-hair.others: Wildflowers exquisite on 6/21/2024.  Jacob's Ladder; Larkspur; Nodding Onion; Indian Paintbrush to name a few!

deer-lake.fullDescription: This hike starts at the T.H. for Sol Duc Falls. Pass Sol Duc Falls and proceed on up to Deer Lake for about 3 miles on a very rocky trail. From Deer Lake @ ~ 3.65 mi., turn off & go on up ~ a mile to the Potholes Meadows Extension along the start of the High Divide Trail @ ~ 4,097' Elevation.   Hit a camp spot at ~ 4.75-5 mi.  https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/map-c2937f3-17 Pros Other

deer-park.fullDescription: Leave from the Deer Park Campground and go towards the Benches passing the 3-Forks Trail @ ~ .3 mi.  Go down to Benches and make a loop coming back up to the Weather Tracking Station that Craig found up on the Ridge and back along the ridge.  Or from Slab Camp, it's about 5.4 mi. R.T. to the Benches and about 1,800' elev. gain. Pros Other
deer-park.others: Could be a Wed. hike or add on Blue Mt. and the Rain Shadow Loop to make it a Fri. hike, so ~ .8 up to Blue Mt. and .5 for the RainShadow Loop.

deer-park---dnr.fullDescription: A DNR area off of Deer Park Rd. not used b many.  Many roads to discover and try!  We did them all!  The upper one has views looking out towards Port Angeles & Ediz Hook. Pros Other
deer-park---dnr.pros: Can also snowshoe here when the snow level is low enough.  We have done about 3 mi. here and gained 455' by parking off side near yellow DNR gate on rt-hand side.
deer-park---dnr.others: Do not do during hunting season.  Also watch for logging.

deer-park-to.fullDescription: This is the eastern end of the Grand Ridge Trail offering incredible views of the Olympics and the Straits of Juan de Fuca. Go up to Maiden Peak @ ~ 6,434' or beyond to the half-way point of Roaring Winds. Experienced drivers for this windy, narrow mountain road needed. Pros Other
deer-park-to.pros: ~ 3.6 mi. & ascent of ~ 1,390' to Maiden Peak.  Another 3/4 mi. to flat spot at ~ 4.5 mi., a good lunch spot.
deer-park-to.others: If go to Roaring Winds, you add about a mile each way and drop down some losing elev; but Roaring Winds is about half-way.  Check stats on this.

discovery.fullDescription: Easy hike off of Diamond Point Road off of Miller Peninsula.  Out-and-back.  Takes about 1-1/2 hours to complete.  Or we can do the Diamond Point Loop Trail, which is shorter.  Get a viewpoint over Discovery Bay.  Very limited parking. Please carpool. Pros Other
discovery.pros: Easy hike when one is short of time.

disc.fullDescription: We start at “Rainshadow Disc Golf club”  No frisbee throwing skills are required, Frisbees  will be supplied and instruction will be offered as needed. It’s just for fun, and the course is beautiful and fun to walk if even if you don’t want to play the entire time. Pros Other

deer-park-dnr.fullDescription: This uses a DNR area off of Deer Park Rd. before the gate (on the right-hand side).  We can snowshoe along the road for a bit and then head left uphill toward the top and to a log landing.  It often offers some good views of Port Angeles and gives a decent workout! Pros Other
deer-park-dnr.pros: Can do this area when the snow level is low enough and when we can't get up to Hurricane Ridge!

dosewallips.fullDescription: This hike is up the Dosewallips River Rd., which turns off before Brinnon.  Hike to the Dosewallips Cascades Falls is 5.5 mi.  Spring is good time to view falls.  Hikers can proceed up to abandoned Ranger Station & Campground another approximate mile, if desired.   https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/washington/dosewallips-river-road-trail Pros Other
dosewallips.pros: Fun side trip is to the big side bridge of 1972 ~ a 1/4 mile  BEFORE the abandoned Elkhorn C.G. at about 2.25 miles.
dosewallips.others: Ramblers say ~ 11 miles to 13 miles and 1,335'-1,650'.  It's about 964' to Cascade Falls

dungeness.fullDescription: There are a total of about 10-15 miles of multi-use trails and routes in this ~400-acre, multi-use area off of River Rd. & Happy Valley Rd. on DNR & also on some tribal land. The hike will include 6 miles of winding trails in the forest, along irrigation canals and down to the Dungeness River. Pros Other

dungeness-fish.fullDescription: Drive from Sequim-Dungeness Fish Hatchery up DNR Rd. to a gate at corner (past a "shooting gallery"),  Park off to side.  Walk ~ @ 1/2 mi. on mellow, uphill grade & then down ~ a mile towards river and the old Clink Bridge, which was built ~150 years' ago.  See remnants of the old bridge that spanned ~ 20-25' across the Dungeness River.  Look across towards other side, which comes down from Burnt Hill.  Tour the Fish Hatchery grounds afterwards, if time permits. Pros Other
dungeness-fish.others: Do not do during hunting season, as this is on DNR land!

dungeness-levee.fullDescription: See the new Lower Dungeness River Floodplain Restoration Levee, which creates better fish habitat by providing more room for the Dungeness River to meander within its floodplain.  This is a pleasant walk where birds may be seen, so bring binoculars!  We leave from parking lot near the historic Dungeness Schoolhouse. Pros Other
dungeness-levee.pros: May be able to see new calves at the Dungeness Creamery!  Also bring $ for ice cream.  Saw ducks, eagle, heron, & a couple of hawks.  Heard lion over at Olympic Game Farm.

dungeness-spit.fullDescription: Walk down ~  1/2 mile from parking at the Dungeness National Wildlife Refuge to the beach & walk on the spit to the New Dungeness Lighthouse for ~ 5 miles.  We plan accordingly to walk/hike at the best minus tide. This is a "must do", if you haven't done it already; or make it an annual tradition! Pros Other
dungeness-spit.others: Get Sarah to give us tidal info.

elbo.fullDescription: This is a moderately difficult hike, especially the first 2.5 miles and then becomes moderate after that point hiking along a F.S. road. There are a couple of viewpoints at ~ the 4-mile mark (Mt. Jupiter, Constance, & the Brothers) and at ~ the 4.5-mile mark, can get views towards Hood Canal & the Cascades. Then, one can continue on up to a cell tower up on Buck Mt. Then, there is a “goat trail” up to a cliff edge for even better views. Pros Other
elbo.pros: May get rhodys on this hike and wildflowers in the late Spring!  Also some saprophytes at about the 2.25-mile stretch in the storm slide section!
elbo.others: This is a good alternative to the too busy and popular Mt. Walker.  Lunch spot gained ~ 2,356' & at 3,259'

elwha.fullDescription: Beach access off of Place Rd. off Hwy. 112. Interesting to see the w. side of the mouth of the Elwha R. and explore the beach seeing where the free-flowing Elwha has gone.  "This sandy beach on the Strait was formed after the dams on the Elwha River were removed in 2011 and 2014, gradually releasing many tons of sediment".  A fun surprise of driftwood sculptures can be seen like "Lone Guardian" (Mac the dog).  One can go to the rt., as well along the west banks of the Elwha.  Bring binoculars for any bird watching. Pros Other

elwha-fish.fullDescription: Walk by the Elwha Fish Hatchery & park under the beautiful pedestrian/car bridge over the Elwha River.  Do a network of trails & roads near the river, past the water pump house & gate.  Plan accordingly to the fish coming up river.  May even see some osprey! Pros Other
elwha-fish.pros: Hit it around Oct. 10th when the Elwha Tribe opens up to fishing.  Very interesting!

elwha-stock.fullDescription: "New" hike for group, as discovered by one of our hikers.  A 1.5-mile section is a "user-built" section on an old pack trail to the Olympic Hot Springs from 1908.  This section has one short, rough portion to negotiate.  There are several variations of this route--either starting from Herrick Rd., Madison Falls, or a car shuttle between the two, or an out-and-back.  Can incorporate the Altair Campground using caution in the slippery mud/clay section.  Bring poles & wear gaiters. Pros Other
elwha-stock.pros: Not busy yet! Did ~ 9.25 & 1,140' on 2/2/2024.  Madison-Altair is 2.5 mi. along water trail. Altair to stock is ~ .75 mi.  Stock is 1.25-1.50.  1 mi. to dam. 1 mi. to Altair. 2.5 mi. to Madison.
elwha-stock.others: Wear gaiters for brushy section; bring poles.  Section is~ 1.25-1.5 miles.  Comes out ~1 mile above Glines.  About 2.5 mi. to Madison from Altaire.  1 mile from dam to Altair.  2.5 miles from Herrick to stock trail.

elwha-rs.fullDescription: This strenuous hike leaves from beyond the Elwha Ranger Station from the beginning of the Whiskey Bend Road.  It is a hike up towards Hurricane Hill on a trail not often used but a very good workout.  Go to the Elwha Overlook (Deer Hair Rock) up about 4 miles before turning around.  Hike is in the trees for the majority of time before opening up into a meadow, which can take some navigation to get through up to Deer Hair Rock. Pros Other
elwha-rs.pros: Not busy; very quiet.  Saw lots of wildflower and saprophytes.  Avg. about 1 mile/hour, as it's a gain of ~ 1,000'/mile (like Heather Park).
elwha-rs.others: Elev. could be as much as 4,554'? (Madison @ 250'/T.H. @ ~ 500' & Deer Hair @ ~ 4400'.  If you go to Hurricane Hill & parking lot, Diane says it's:  10.5 mi. & 6,800'! (I get 5 ,354).

falls.fullDescription: This hike is south of 101 from Quilcene and before Mt. Walker.  It leaves from a newly reopened Falls View Campground.  Can view an unnamed ribbon waterfall that falls ~ 100' from an easy trail near the campground called Falls View.  From there, a trail drops 200' in about .1 mile into the canyon to the big Quilcene River.  Can cross a bridge and follow the roaring river upstream.  Before a 1/2 mile is a bench to enjoy the surroundings.  Beyond that is a 1/2 mile loop trail. Pros Other

foothills.fullDescription: This multi-use, DNR area off of Little River Road, provides a network of trails, including On Ramp, Quick Climb, Sunny Side, Freefall, Phantom Bear, I-5, Water World, the Shire, E. Phantom Bear, just to name a few.  On top, at a picnic table for lunch, we hope to get good views of P.A., the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and back to Mt. Angeles, First Top, and Blue Mt. to the south, etc. Pros Other
foothills.pros: Many loops and possibilities here.  One can get over 11 miles on this network of trails.

fort.fullDescription: Built in 1856 at Port Townsend Bay. It has Army history, including a torpedo x-ray tower and an abandoned military cemetery (27 bodies were removed in 1898).  Many lovely forested trails: a bluff, rhody, madrona, fern, and trillium trails, native plants, and self-guided interpretive history trail. Pros Other
fort.pros: Evergreen Huckleberry & Mushroom were good in mid-Oct.!

fort-flagler.fullDescription: Walk bluff trail, etc. at this fort (on the N. tip of Marrowstone Island), including around lagoon and at upper campground on return trail. Sometimes, we are even able to walk along the beach getting stunning views!   May even see paragliders, see the abandoned military gun emplacements, batteries, etc. Can start at the Wansboro Battery where there are Restrooms. Pros Other
fort-flagler.others: North tip of Marrowstone Island.  Watch the tides.  Wed. hike

fort-wordenn.fullDescription: Walk along the beach from N. Beach to the Point Wilson Lighthouse for ~ 2 miles.  Hike through Fort Worden going to the Memory's Vault, on Artillery Hill passing some of the batteries, through a tunnel, and then on the Chinese Gardens Trail!  Or' can hike Ft. Worden in other areas, as well! Pros Other
fort-wordenn.others: Check tides.  Regular Ft. Worden is ~ 5-7 miles and 400-700'

gibbs.fullDescription: There are many loops & hiking options here. One popular route is around the lake in this 700-acre County Park in Jefferson County. The Walt Hoffman Trail (with peekaboo views of the 90-acre lake) & possible add-ons of Jack’s Track Trail, Springboard, Ameri-Corps, Scout's Trail add a nice variety.  There is a convenient picnic table and restroom at the lake for a snack and lunch. Pros Other
gibbs.pros: Ramblers & Diane have done a Mon. hike here. We did this on 4/10 & added on Roller Coaster and Impossi-Bowl on the outer loop and then Springboard. It was more like 500'
gibbs.others: Mushrooms in Fall.  Leaves off trees for more views of the lake in Feb.  Can also get more mileage for a Friday hike and can get up to 9 mi. & ~730' when no logging!

gibson.fullDescription: Good views from here of Travis Spit, Protection Island, Washington Harbor, and the mts. Pros Other
gibson.others: Low Tide.  Respect the private property and bridge going over to the Pacific NW Natl. Lab.

glass.fullDescription:
Glass Beach is known for its beach glass.  ~ 3 miles to McCurdy Point. 
Access from North Beach parking lot off of Kuhn St. in Port Townsend. A forked weeder comes in handy if beach glass collection is your thing. There is a nice minus tide around noon which will make much more of the beach accessible. Pros Other
glass.pros: Views of Cascades, Mt. Baker, Whidbey Island, and the San Juans.  Known for sea glass from refuge dumped at McCurdy Point into the Strait about 60 years' ago.  Some cobblestone to negotiate.
glass.others: Only do this when the tides are below 6 ft. and falling.  Bring small containers or baggies for collecting any sea glass and a small rake.

glines.fullDescription: This hike goes up to the Glines Canyon Dam Overlook (Dam removed in 2014) using the Bypass Trail & heading up the Whiskey Bend Rd. Hikers can also explore the Lake Mills Trail near the spillway, go up to Windy Arm, or up to the end of the road to the Whiskey Bend T.H. Pros Other

glines-canyon.fullDescription: This hike starts at madison falls and goes up to the Glines Canyon Dam Overlook (Dam removed in 2014) using the Bypass Trail & heading up the Whiskey Bend Rd. Pros Other

goa.fullDescription: Up just before the old Schoolhouse on Blue Mt. Road.  On DNR land on the left opposite of GOA Rd. Can get some loops off from here!  Some "peekaboo" views towards the mts.  Can also go down to McDonald Creek, which is on the opposite side of the shorter Cassidy Creek loop! Pros Other
goa.others: Don't do in the Fall? 1 mile to main intersection.  4 miles to McDonald Creek on the way back.  Wear long pants and long sleeves because of possible "stinging nettles".

gold.fullDescription: Trail starts at the Lower Dungeness. Cross an old road bridge across the Dungeness at ~1/2 mile.  Turn right.  Cross Gold Creek at a mile.  Follow the Lower Dungeness Canyon up fairly steep to at least the Sleepy Hollow junction at ~ 3-1/2 mi. after climbing rather steeply a mile after crossing Sleepy Hollow Creek! The Gold Creek Trail proceeds another 3-1/2 mi. to the end of the trail across from the Tubal Cain T.H.--a 14-mile R.T. hike. There are some steep grades of up to 20%. Pros Other

gold-creek.fullDescription: Starts at (47.972308, -123.100532) off of Palo Alto road. Goes down to where the Gold Creek shelter was, close to the cement bridge. Where the old campground was.  Easy walk, a couple of small water crossings. https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/washington/gold-creek-extension-trail Pros Other

grannys.fullDescription: This walk/hike is along DNR State Forest Rd. (PA J-1000) west of Granny's Café.  Walk along the road heading East.  Road joins up to Karpen Rd. from the other end letting us connect-the-dots from what we do from that end off of Dan Kelly Rd.! Pros Other
grannys.others: Just avoid hunting season in mid-Oct. to end Oct. & 4 days in Nov.  Big gravel prevented us from hiking earlier.  Watch for logging activity?

griff.fullDescription: The steep trail leaves from behind the Elwha Ranger Station @ ~ 2.1 mi.; & it climbs up, equating to about 1,000’/mile (considered difficult)! At ~1.5 miles, you come to a large rock with your first viewpoint towards Elwha Valley. Less than a ½ mile further, is a 2nd viewpoint--a good turn-around point. Pros Other
griff.pros: Views; Marilyn Snook says that it is up to 9.25 mi. & 3,800'?  2,800' in 3 mi.  Views of Griff, Unicorn, and Hurricane Hill
griff.others: Difficult  proceeding past the 2nd overlook.  Gets much rougher w/several downed trees to trail end & ~ 800'/last 1/2 mi..  Up to 10 mi./3,000'.  2.8 miles to trail end.

griff-creek.fullDescription: This is a unique route to go to the Griff Creek T.H. from behind the Elwha R.S. from what is the traditional route.  This adds more mileage and elevation gain.  Start on the W. Elwha R. Trail from Herrick Rd., hike the 3 miles to the old Altaire C.G.; cross the Elwha on Olympic Hot Springs Rd., hike down to the Elwha R.S..  Hike proceeds up a steep ascent to a 1st overlook after ~ 1-1/2 miles.  Great lunch spot or can go an addtl. ~ 3/4 mi. to 2nd overlook.  Retrace steps back to car. Pros Other

grindstone.fullDescription: Grindstone Flats/Meadow turn-off is ~ a 1/2 mile beyond Camp Handy along the Dungeness River.  Go to the right at a trail juncturento the Heather Basin Trail for ~ a mile.  Drop down to Grindstone Flats, which is in a meadow and quite pleasant along the creek.  One can proceed on up the valley towards Heather Basin along the Heather Creek Trail # 863; but Grindstone Flats/Meadow is usually the turn-around point. Pros Other

grand.fullDescription: Go from the end of Obstruction Point Rd. to Roaring Winds and back.  Go in July or later when the one steep snowfield is safe to cross.  The views are grand--therefore the name for this trail--the highest in the Olympics.  Enjoy "craggy, glacier-covered peaks, deep, emerald valleys, and miles of wildflowers, and alpine tundra".  Can also go an extra .6 mi. & ~ 300' up to top of Elk Mt. The scree slope beyond Elk Mt. cut-off can be rather intimidating and dangerous.  Experienced drivers for this windy, narrow mountain road needed. Pros Other
grand.pros: If you do as a key exchange; it's about 7.8 mi. & 2,306' (east to west) & 1,223 (west to east).
grand.others: Can do this as a possible Wed. hike.  Just need capable drivers for this!

guillemot.fullDescription: This 184-acre reserve is near Seabeck and offers walking trails and even some saltwater beach access.  Can follow an access road through an alder and big leaf maple tree forest or on a Sawmill Trail.  A popular stop is to the Stump House (a large, hollowed out cedar stump with a roof)! Pros Other

heart.fullDescription: This is a pleasant nature trail leaving from Loop "E" in the Heart of the Hills Campground @ ~ 1,400'. It offers beautiful, old-growth trees, plenty of fern varieties, and other flora in a rainforest-type ecosystem.  While hiking on this trail, carefully cross puncheon walkways, as they can be slippery.  Hikers go to a big, fallen tree above Lake Creek, which makes a good turn-around point before leaving the Natl. Park boundary. Pros Other
heart.others: Hike starts at the "E" Loop @ about 1,400' elev.  Restrooms at the Loop A are heated and usually open and can usually park at the parking lot in above there!

heather.fullDescription: Hike starts at same parking lot as the Lake Angeles hike. Trail climbs a steep ridge; passes 1/2-Way Rock (not quite 1/2 way) @ 2.2 mi.!  Pass an old stone fireplace structure built in 1938 (Heather Park Forest Camp) on a side trail @ 5,300'. Go through a sub-alpine, heather basin known as Heather Park @ ~ 4.1 mi. w/creek and campsites.  Go by a prominent pinnacle known as 2nd Top. Make final climb to Heather Pass for good views of the Strait and Mt. Olympus. Pros Other
heather.pros: Past 1/2 way rock there is another rock or viewpoint on left at ~ 3.1 mi. & 2,770' gain before stone fireplace.
heather.others: Fall Colors can be great up there!

hurricane.fullDescription: Don’t miss this chance for views of the Bailey Range while also getting a good workout up this newly paved trail to the top of Hurricane Hill at 5757'.  You might even get a chance to see deer, bear, or the Olympic marmot!  The wildflowers can also be quite lovely! Pros Other
hurricane.pros: It's ~ .25 to the top from the Elwha turn-off (map says .1!).  We even walked in there for a view!  Distance also depends upon where you can park.  Add when from picnic area.
hurricane.others: Wed. hike.  ONP V.I.C. states that it's 3.2 mi. R.T. & 700' gain.

hurricane-ridge.fullDescription: Can follow road from Hurricane Ridge parking area and go at least to the picnic area w/ opportunities for viewing the Olympics along the way! From the picnic area, it is advised that only the more experienced snowshoers proceed & head up towards Hurricane Hill after they have a brief avalanche presentation.  Drivers are required to carry tire chains in their vehicle and be competent driving in snow/icy conditions.  We also have other options of snowshoeing, as well. Pros Other
hurricane-ridge.others: Potential avalanche up towards Hurricane Hill. It is advised that if you are going to be snowshoeing in avalanche terrain that you take a Basic Avalanche Awareness Course.

joyce-piedmont.fullDescription: Leave from Joyce-Piedmont Rd. and head West on the Olympic Adventure Trail (West).  This is also called the Crescent Descent, as it heads to Lake Crescent and can end up at the Spruce R.R.  Follow the Lyre River Road a bit, to the Lyre River Bridge, and can even see Lyre River Falls from up above (or before the bridge)! Pros Other
joyce-piedmont.pros: Nice lunch spot down near lake before getting to the Spruce RR parking.  Can go to the Spruce RR area and use bathrooms before turning around
joyce-piedmont.others: Can get quite muddy and there may be some logging activity.  (Earlier, Terri said that it was 1,200' gain).

karpen.fullDescription: This hike is on Karpen Rd./State Forest Road off of Dan Kelly Road.  Can combine with part of the OAT Trail, as well, to make a fun loop going by the Living Room and back to the road! Pros Other
karpen.others: Paul showed us this loop, which is new to us.  Hit L.R. @ ~ 2.3 mi. and then to Karpen about a mile later and back to parking!

kloshe.fullDescription: Hike before Forks and south of Mt. Muller on Snider Ridge.  Follow Sol Duc River for short distance (~ 1/4 mi.) before heading up on the trail, which climbs steadily through ~ 30 switchbacks & crossing 3 small creeks.  On a clear day, it offers fabulous views of Sol Duc Valley, Mt. Appleton, Mt. Tom, & Mt. Olympus from a viewing platform that used to be a fire lookout tower until 1965 & then a replica from 1996-2012.  Kloshe Nanitch is Chinook for "standing guard".  Go up to the platform, up a road, and then do a loop to N. Point and back around to the trail. Pros Other
kloshe.pros: Not very busy.  Can add 1.2 miles on the N. Point loop trail that connects with Snider Ridge Trail and back around.  Kloshe is at about 3,137'-3,160'
kloshe.others: May encounter "nudist" in area.  If you proceed along Snider Ridge to Jim's Junction on the Mt. Muller Trail, it is about 9 miles total.  3 miles to Jim's Junction.

kloshe-nanitch.fullDescription: Hike before Forks and south of Mt. Muller on Snider Ridge.  Follow Sol Duc River for short distance (~ 1/4 mi.) before heading up on the trail, which climbs steadily through ~ 30 switchbacks & crossing 3 small creeks.  On a clear day, it offers fabulous views of Sol Duc Valley, Mt. Appleton, Mt. Tom, & Mt. Olympus from a viewing platform that used to be a fire lookout tower until 1965 & then a replica from 1996-2012.  Kloshe Nanitch is Chinook for "standing guard".  Go up to the platform, up a road, and then do a loop to N. Point and back around to the trail. Pros Other
kloshe-nanitch.pros: Not very busy.  Can add 1.2 miles on the N. Point loop trail that connects with Snider Ridge Trail and back around.  Kloshe is at about 3,137'-3,160'
kloshe-nanitch.others: May encounter "nudist" in area.  If you proceed along Snider Ridge to Jim's Junction on the Mt. Muller Trail, it is about 9 miles total.  3 miles to Jim's Junction.

lake.fullDescription: Lake Angeles is a very popular & busy, 3.7-mile hike up to a beautiful, 20-acre, alpine lake in a "glacier-sculpted landscape".  Parking lot is before the Hurricane Ridge Guard Station and shares parking with the Heather Park T.H.  After crossing Ennis Creek at ~ 1 mile, hike continues to climb steadily to the lake.  Stop at the lake or proceed up an addtl. ~1.5 miles and ~ 1,000’ to the Lake Angeles Overlook to look down at the lake and be able to see where you have climbed! s Pros Other

lake-angelesheather.fullDescription: This is a difficult hike that should only be done by experienced hikers.  Can either go clockwise or counter-clockwise.  If clockwise, go up to the Lake Angeles Overlook & Klahane Ridge to Victor Pass & up to No Name Pass and then Heather Park Pass near 2nd Top & then back down towards the Lake Angeles/Heather Park parking lot making this a loop.  A couple of "dicey" scree slopes that can make it rather sketchy.  Use caution! Pros Other
lake-angelesheather.pros: Great views of the Strait, the Olympics, etc.
lake-angelesheather.others: Do as an Ad Hoc hike.  This is not for every one.  One slip could be dangerous. Some prefer clockwise, if stronger leg is on downhill side in sketchy part near No-Name Pass.

larry.fullDescription: This portion of the Larry Scott Trail leaves off of 733 Cape George Rd. & goes to the Boat Yard (Boathaven) in Port Townsend.  It goes by the road, residences, and along Hwy. 20.  There are ways to get off the trail onto the horse trails, which is less "jarring".  Also pass the Port Townsend Paper Mill that was built in 1928.  May see heron along the waterfront and a metal leaf statue before hitting the Boat Yard. Pros Other
larry.pros: Sani-can at Cape George but no apparent R.R. at the Boat Yard.  Can sit on logs for a snack or return a bit to a small point where there are a couple of picnic tables.

larry-scott.fullDescription: Can go from Milo Curry T.H. near 4-Corners to Cape George off of Discovery Rd. near Port Townsend and return while passing through horse country and pleasant surroundings! The Larry Scott Trail is to be the beginning of the Olympic Discovery Trail (ODT) and is also part of the Pacific N.W. Scenic Trail!  Total Larry Scott Trail is ~7.3 mi. one way.  It is named for a Port Townsend resident and cycling enthusiast who played an important part in the trail. Pros Other
larry-scott.pros: There is a forest reserve near Cape George Rd.  that had a trail.  We enjoyed that.  There are a few ways off of that trail; but we stayed on the main.
larry-scott.others: Sani-cans @  Milo-Curry & Cape George.  More parking at Cape George. Go from Cape George (733 Cape George Rd.) to Port Townsend next time, which is 3.7 mi. one way.

lena.fullDescription: This is a popular hike, as it is relatively short to Lower Lena Lake but with a large, sub-alpine lake as a destination. Enjoy lunch at a large picnic rock overlooking the lake or at a couple of campspots beyond.  Climb some long, flat switchbacks to get to the lake.  After lunch, we may proceed on a loop towards The Brothers Trail passing campsites and then return back to the trail on a loop Pros Other
lena.others: Ramblers say 3.8 one way & 1,450' & up to the end 1,717' & 7+ mi. (On 5/3, it was 4 miles to big rock after doing loop & 1,400').

little.fullDescription: Trail is out of the Sol Duc area.  It can be done in a clockwise or counter-clockwise direction with a car shutte at the Mink Lake T.H. at Sol Duc Resort and other car at the Sol Duc Falls T.H.  Hike is on rocky, rooty terrain and is considered moderate-to-difficult.  One passes Deer Lake and then is on more seldom used LIttle Divide Trail, over to the Bogachiel River drainage intersection, and on down to Mink Lake, and back to the Sol Duc Resort, or vice-versa. Pros Other
little.others: Meadow at 6.2 miles for lunch going clockwise direction.  Takes about 7 hours

lillian.fullDescription: Enjoy majestic mountain panoramas from this relatively low-effort, high-vista hike on the Olympic Peninsula.  https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/lillian-ridge Pros Other

little-humpbig.fullDescription: Little Hump and down to the camps along the river is at ~ 2.4 mi./700'. Then, if one wishes to proceed, there are ~ 16 short switchbacks & an ~800’-1,000' climb to Big Hump or "Snack Rock" ?)"ledges where one can survey the wild valley & Saint Peters Dome to the south") at ~ 3.9 mi. and then a substantial 1.4 mi./600' drop to the river at the 5.3-mile River Camp.  "Marvel at the wild river, as it tumbles over giant boulders and squeezes through narrow, rocky clefts."  If time allows, one could stop and hike to Murhut and Ranger Hole, as well. Pros Other
little-humpbig.pros: WILDERNESS AT 1.2 Mi.  EARLY START!  Check these stats!  It is 10.6 mi. to 5-Mile Camp & 2,300' according to WTA.  Beth got the figure above, which is 2,776'  Big Hump is wilderness
little-humpbig.others: If go to Little Hump & down to the river alone, that is about 5.8 mi. and 1,100'.  Murhut is ~ 1.6 mi. & 278-300'  Ranger Hole is ~ 1.85 mi. and 265-292'.

little-humpmurhut.fullDescription: Little Hump and down to the camps along the river is at ~ 2.4 mi./700'., then drive to Murhut falls.  This is a beautiful, 2-tiered (one tier at ~120' & the other at ~ 35' for a total of 155') waterfall is in a narrow ravine up the Duckabush River.  One may also see some native Pacific rhodies enroute! Trail starts on an old logging road for a short climb of ~250' and then drops down 50' into a ravine.  A further option is Rocky Brook falls Pros Other
little-humpmurhut.pros: Do it in May when the waterfall is at the highest.  Saw lots of trillium, some dogwood, and bleeding heart.

little-river.fullDescription: This is a hike close to Port Angeles off of the Black Diamond Rd. The trail enters Natl. Park at about 1.2 miles. This used to be a historical trail leading to mines. You will pass by rock walls, old growth trees, and cross log bridges across the S. Branch of the Little River about 5-7 times and can end up at a log bridge (with a rope for support). Pros Other
little-river.pros: Can be a Wed. or Fri. hike.  A Wed. hike would be to Little River Falls @ ~ 2-1/2 mi. & 540' or to 4th bridge another mile and ~ 800' for 7.5 miles. (see below too),  ~7 bridges
little-river.others: Cowan Creek at 2 miles; Little River Falls at ~ 2.5 miles.  ~7 mi. R.T. to 4th bridge at ~ 875'  Ramblers say that it is 8.8 mi. R.T. to rope bridge and ~ 1,745' cum. or 1,050' net.

louella.fullDescription: Starts at the parking area up from Louella Cabin. Loops include hikes to the Dungeness River, 5-ravine crossing, Pat's Hill, Beck Hill, well-house trail, and broken-bridge trail all in various combinations. Pros Other

lovers.fullDescription: Loop from Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort up to Sol Duc Falls and back through the Campground or in reverse!  Enjoy the "lush bottomlands and groves of impressive ancient trees" plus some mushrooms and the water of Sol Duc River and Canyon Creek.  Afterwards, a stop will be made down the road at the Salmon Cascades to view the salmon jumping the falls--quite a spectacular feat! Pros Other

lower.fullDescription: View the W. Elwha Dam Site, which was removed in 2012 (old Lake Aldwell). Parking from either Karpen Rd. or the OAT Horse Parking near Colville Mt. Bike area off Dan Kelly Rd. and off Hwy. 112.  Can make it a loop utilizing Karpen Rd. and the OAT Trail.  There will be a couple of rough sections, so poles will be helpful, as you must have agility to cross saplings and a couple of steep sections.  Wear gaiters for wet brush.  A surprise will be shown near the old dam and spillway! Pros Other

lower-dungeness.fullDescription: Starts at Lower parking lot of Lower Dungeness T.H. off F.S. Rd. 2860. Follows the Dungeness & then climbs steadily up from the river valley to the 3 O'Clock Ridge Trail, a good turn-around & half-way mark after crossing Skookum & Cougar Creeks.  Or, can continue towards the historic River Camp Shelter crossing Bungalow Creek or even further on to the Upper Dungeness area crossing Mueller Creek.   May get views of Mt. Worthington & Mt. Fricaba from "Pride Rock". Pros Other
lower-dungeness.pros: 1,645'.  I got ~ 5.75 miles and ~ 1,350' on 2/12/2024.  See file on this lower section.  ~ .7 to upper T.H. for lower section.  ~ 2.14 mi.-Cougar Creek.  2.5 mi. Pride Rock; 2nd rock.

lower-dungeness---upper.fullDescription: Trail is the upper part of the Lower Dungeness trail, which is across from the Upper Dungeness Trail system.  Hike goes down along the Dungeness River to the River Shelter at ~ 1.85 mi. after crossing a slide area (476').  Can proceed on the trail, crossing Bungalow Creek and can go up to 3 O'Clock Ridge on 4 switchbacks, a good turn-around and half-way point for the trail. Pros Other
lower-dungeness---upper.pros: Not a busy trail like the Upper Dungeness.  Can see Rattlesnake Plantain if you hit it right!  We did on Sept. 20th.

oldlower.fullDescription: Distance will be dependent upon which trailhead is used and if the Cat Creek Loop (~ 1.4 mi.) is used. Enjoy this hike along/near the Gray Wolf River with its many features.  One comes down to the river 2-3 times at Two-Mile Camp, Cliff Camp, etc., and also goes up above the river in spots. TH(47.965852050902726, -123.11529467667314).  Google maps wrong. Pros Other
oldlower.pros: Spring flowers like chocolate lilies up at the one viewpoint, trillium, etc.  Elev. of 1,950'?
oldlower.others: Do not go beyond the last camp and slide where bridge was washed out in the early 1990's.  GROUP SIZE OF 12 at the WILDERNESS @ the 1.5 - 2 mile mark.

lower-big.fullDescription: This hike goes down along the Big Quilcene River from the Ten-Mile Shelter at the Marmot Pass T.H. Parking Lot. It passes Camp Jolly & goes towards Bark Shanty. It offers solitude & perhaps some berry picking! Pros Other

lower-big-quilcene.fullDescription: This hike starts along the Lower Big Quilcene River from the Lower Quilcene trailhead and follows along an old roadbed (sometimes called the "Champagne Trail") amongst both young forest and old-growth cedar trees.  We’ll turn around at Bark Shanty, the 1st established campsite right along the river or continue past the slide bypass. Pros Other
lower-big-quilcene.pros: Can go from Marmot parking lot down to Bark Shanty passing Camp Jolly at 1.5 mi. & Bark Shanty @ ~ 3.8 mi. Reverse hike & about 1,136' ascent back.  Some berries!
lower-big-quilcene.others: Wed. hike to Bark Shanty; otherwise an easy to moderate Fri. hike if to Camp Jolly.  If you go all the way up to the road, it is ~13 mi. R.T. and 1,890'.  To Bark Shanty is 2.7 mi.

lyre.fullDescription: Conservation area is E. of Joyce and off of Reynolds Rd.  280 acres have been conserved by the N. Olympic Land Trust on the east side of the mouth of the Lyre River.  Area offers mature, 2nd- growth forest; streams; tide flats; and a 1/2 mile stretch along the Strait of Juan de Fuca shoreline.  Bring binoculars for bird viewing!  After doing a loop on this trail of going down to the Strait, can come back and cross over to the DNR Campground and walk along the river a bit. Pros Other

madison.fullDescription: Walk on the E. side of the Elwha River from Madison Falls, up along the Bypass Trail, by the Elwha Ranger Station, on the Olympic Hot Springs Rd.  crossing the Elwha River. & down to the abandoned Altair Campground. Pros Other

madison-falls.fullDescription: Go from Madison Falls parking lot, up past Elwha Ranger Station, up past the abandoned Altair Campground to Glines Canyon Dam.  From the west side of the dam, head towards the old boat launch for Lake Mills, walk out onto lake bed, find a suitable place for lunch and look for lupine. Pros Other
madison-falls.pros: Look for lupine, Nootka rose, and asters as planted by Sarah and the Turnbergs!  We did it on June 2nd.  Do a little bit earlier maybe around Memorial Day!

madison-falls-to.fullDescription: Hike goes from Madison Falls parking, use Bypass Trail or Water Edge Trail (if safe), pass the Elwha Ranger Station at 2 miles, left up Whiskey Bend Rd. to Glines Canyon Dam at ~ 3.5 mi. Proceed on up to Windy Arm at 4.5 mi. and proceed on up to end of Whiskey Bend Rd. at ~7 miles. Pros Other
madison-falls-to.pros: Good, long hike but fairly easy.
madison-falls-to.others: If turn around at Windy Arm, it is ~ 9.25 mi. R.T. & 900' elev. gain.  Terri got 2,051' Debbie got 1,959.  Ramblers got 2,171!  What? I got 1,052'

marmot.fullDescription: This is one of the more difficult, but popular, hikes in the area steadily climbing up to Marmot Pass at ~ 6,000'. There are wonderful views from up on top with a steep, ¾-mile climb up to this point from Camp Mystery. The trail follows the Upper Big Quilcene River, goes by Shelter Rock Camp, leaving the river at Camp Mystery at ~ 4.6 miles and on up the final ascent to Marmot Pass, which "captures what makes the Olympics so special". Pros Other
marmot.others: Shelter Rock Camp @ 2.6 mi. and ~ 1,300'; Camp Mystery at 4.6 mi.;  WILDERNESS of 12.

marymere.fullDescription: Enjoy this popular, picturesque waterfall. Add on by hiking to the 1st bridge at Barnes Creek and then the “Moments in Time”/Barnes Point Trail for some variety. Pros Other
marymere.others: 1st Bridge up Barnes Creek is at 1.4 miles.  "Moments in Time" Trail is ~ 1/3 - 1/2 mile.

mount.fullDescription: It starts by the river gage on the elwha.  It's steep and will have ice and snow on it.  48.05478018,	-123.5832136 Pros Other

miller.fullDescription: Starts at Diamond Pt parking lot.  Go West to W Diamond point trail.  Stay on west edge of park. Connect with Aerospace road and proceed to Discovery bay loop.  Return by diamond point trail.  https://www.strava.com/activities/15663013666 Pros Other

miller-peninsula.fullDescription: Hiking route is from E. Sequim Bay Rd. & follows the Manzanita/Bluff Trail.  Pleasant hike in coastal woods & offers plenty of solitude on this multi-use trail system! 	https://www.alltrails.com/explore/recording/afternoon-hike-f7ac67a-146 Pros Other

miller-1.fullDescription: Many routes & options are at this State Park, depending upon what the leader chooses, whether it be from E. Sequim Bay Road, along the Manzanita/Bluff Trail; off of Pierce Road; or from the main parking area off of Diamond Point Rd.; to the beach, to Captain Thompson's grave, etc. Pros Other
miller-1.others: ~ 4.75 to 5.5 mi. from E. Sequim Bay Rd. & ~ 338'-350' up to 750' if Mickie leads a Wed. hike.  She went to the beach once and got 8 mi. & 788' or 7.5 mi. & 423' if go to Beach.

miller-peninsula-to.fullDescription: This out-and-back starts at the Diamond point parking lot, and proceeds to Thompson Spit. Pros Other

mink.fullDescription: This trail leaves from Sol Duc Hot Springs. A shelter at Mink Lake allows for a good turn-around point. Fish may be seen jumping in the lake and perhaps some huckleberries will be alongside the trail on your return trip! Rocky, Rooty trail Pros Other

marymere-fallsmoments.fullDescription: Easy hike near Lake Crescent Lodge.  Add on by going up Barnes Creek Trail to 1st bridge, come back & do the Marymere Falls Trail, go towards Lake Crescent Lodge and Bovee's Meadow, then on the 2/3-mi. Moments of Time Nature Trail.  Go by the Nature Bridge Camp.  The "Moments in Time" self-guided, nature trail (with signs offering history of the area, etc.) used to be called the Barnes Point Nature Trail.  It takes you along the lakeshore, through mature forest, & past a meadow (old homestead).  Leave & go west from the Storm King Ranger Station parking lot. Pros Other
marymere-fallsmoments.others: Can go west (left) from the restrooms.

mt.fullDescription: Drive to end of Mt. Angeles Rd. and park.  Walk up decommissioned road for about 1.5 mi. ending at Hurricane Ridge Rd. & Lake Dawn.  Can go through Heart of Hills C.G. & do Heart of Forest Trail 2.5 mi. to Natl. Park Service Boundary & around to Lake Dawn, if a loop is desired. Pros Other
mt.others: May also visit Ennis Creek Falls and come out through Lake Dawn by Klahhane Cabin.

mount-angeles.fullDescription: This hike will begin at the now lost Hurricane Ridge Lodge and follow the Klahhane Ridge Trail (also known as Sunrise Ridge) to a meadow at the base of Mt Angeles. The trailhead is at the beginning of the lodge parking lot. When leaving the parking lot, we will make a steep but short ascent to the top of a knoll before beginning a hike that can best be described as up-and-down for approximately 2.3 miles to the Mt Angeles trail junction. From there it's a steep climb for .5 miles to the meadow below Mt Angeles. This is a great place for lunch. Pros Other
mount-angeles.others: Wed. hike.  ONP V.I.C. states that it's 3.2 mi. R.T. & 700' gain.

mt-angeles.fullDescription: Access from near Walking Horse Lane about 3 miles up S. Mt. Angeles Rd.  Limited parking for 2-3 cars along roadway.  Do not block the gate.  Paved for about 1/4 mi. to near bridge built in 1969.  Then, gravel/dirt--old logging road.  Follow for about 1.75 mi. to juncture to the Mt. Angeles Connector to the Foothills Trail system (~ .4 mi.).  Can do a number of loops on this system after hitting the Foothills area, including E. Bench Pros Other
mt-angeles.pros: Don't see many folks on this trail.  Paul showed me another loop off of E. Bench?
mt-angeles.others: Do not do In the Fall during hunting season.  (From 1,332--2,668') (~ 1,500'& 4+ mi.)

mt-muller.fullDescription: Trail climbs steeply from LIttleton's Camp at 2,200’ in ~ 2.5 miles to Jim’s Junction. The trail then weaves up/down for 4 mi. along a ridgeline w/ occasional views of Mt. Olympus, Lake Crescent, and the Sol Duc Valley. Pass other spots like Millsap Meadow, Thomas Gap, Jasmine Meadow & New Divide Trail, side trail to official Mt. Muller, Panorama Point, Cahill's Overlook,  Mosely Gap, and Fout's Rock House.  If lucky, we will also see some wildflowers and bear grass up on top! Pros Other
mt-muller.pros: Best in June to see Beargrass and other wildflowers

mt-pleasant.fullDescription: Hike on east end of P.A. off of Monroe and Baker Street, which is west side of Mt. Pleasant.  Multi-use DNR area and mt. bike area.  Get views of the Strait of Juan de Fuca and towards Hurricane Ridge Road! Pros Other

mt-townsend.fullDescription: May do the less traditional and less busy approach up Mt. Townsend: either the Little Quilcene Trail #835 from over Bon Jon Pass or the Dirty Face Ridge approach across from Tubal Cain.  If do the normal approach, climb steadily for 3 mi.; left at Silver Lake junction looking west to Silver Creek Valley at a small gap and then follow couple switchbacks down to valley below and ascend up to Silver Lake. Pros Other
mt-townsend.pros: Little Quilcene Trail over Little River Summit from Bon Jon Pass:  Shortest @~ 7.5-7.8 mi. & 2,100'/2,231'/2,315'/2,475'. 15-20% grade.  (Check stats)
mt-townsend.others: Customize this one depending upon which approach is taken.

mt-townsend-835.fullDescription: We'll do the less busy approach up Mt. Townsend via the Little Quilcene Trail #835 from Bon Jon Pass. Phlox should be blooming and views in the last third of the hike and at the top are fabulous on a clear day.   Of the multiple approaches up Mount Townsend, this option has the shortest distance with the least elevation gain Pros Other
mt-townsend-835.pros: Little Quilcene Trail over Little River Summit from Bon Jon Pass:  Shortest @~ 7.5-7.8 mi. & 2,100'/2,231'/2,315'/2,475'. 15-20% grade.  (Check stats)
mt-townsend-835.others: Customize this one depending upon which approach is taken.

mt-townsend-from.fullDescription: May do the less traditional and less busy approach up Mt. Townsend: either the Little Quilcene Trail #835 from over Bon Jon Pass or the Dirty Face Ridge approach across from Tubal Cain.  If do the normal approach, climb steadily for 3 mi.; left at Silver Lake junction looking west to Silver Creek Valley at a small gap and then follow couple switchbacks down to valley below and ascend up to Silver Lake. Pros Other
mt-townsend-from.pros: Little Quilcene Trail over Little River Summit from Bon Jon Pass:  Shortest @~ 7.5-7.8 mi. & 2,100'/2,231'/2,315'/2,475'. 15-20% grade.  (Check stats)
mt-townsend-from.others: Customize this one depending upon which approach is taken.

mt-walker.fullDescription: Although this is a short hike, it is steep & considered Moderate to Difficult! You can hike up the steep 2-miles to Mt. Walker and see the views of Mt. Constance and the Olympics from the 1st viewpoint and then walk ~ a 1/2 mile along the Summit Rd. to the 2nd viewpoint looking towards Puget Sound & Hood Canal and the N. Cascades and then walk down the road on a much gentler grade for 4 miles back to parking. Pros Other
mt-walker.pros: Do it in May when the rhodys are in bloom!

mt-zion.fullDescription: This trail offers one of the quickest & shortest ascents of ~ 1.8 mi. to a summit in the Olympic Mts.  One passes a site of an old fire lookout built in 1935 and can proceed on to another rock outcrop/overlook after ~ a 1/2 mile for better views of Mt. Townsend and Gray Wolf Ridge.  May see lovely blooms of the Pacific rhody. Pros Other

n.fullDescription: This is a quiet hike off of Sol Duc Rd., as it is one of the least used hikes in the Park!  It the N. Fork of the Sol Duc River with its scenic pools.  Bring water shoes and trekking poles for one major crossing at 1.3 mile.  Wed Hike turns around just before steep hill at 3.8 mi. Pros Other
n.pros: Very nice, quiet hike!  Can swim or dip into the lovely pools.
n.others: Gain 400' in that 1st mile.  Parking for about 6 vehicles off of the Sol Duc Rd.

ned.fullDescription: Site of a former fire lookout tower built in 1933 & one of few remaining lookout structures on the Olympic Peninsula (there in the 80's).  You can still see some of the structure.  A Maynard Peak fire burned the area in 1935, including the structure.  It is a short hike; but a good workout!  Hike through salal & OR grape.  Several tree types are here including pine.  Many Rhodys that are lovely when in bloom!  4 benches on this hike built by a Jim Halvorson and Jim Sanderson, along with the reopening of this "historic" trail some time ago. Pros Other
ned.pros: Very close to the Slap Camp T.H. (~ 1/2 mile away).  Bench at ~ 1/2 mile, .69 mi. & 1 mile (good lunch spot).  Another bench off to rt. in salal!  Couple of logs to go over.
ned.others: Did it on 3/15/2024 & 5/29/2024.  Start at ~ 2,600' & go up to 3,460'.  Off of F.S. Rd. 2878.  Rhodies should be out in ~ mid-June.  They were just starting in late May/2024.

newberry.fullDescription: This park located s.w. of Silverdale off of Newberry Hill Rd. off of Hwy. 3 offers ~ 13 miles of trails like Big Cedar, Alder Pass, Beaver Loop, Bobcat Run, Deer Loop.  We hope to see some rhodies on the Rhodie Hill trail.  If not, we will enjoy features on the many other trails like Salal Ridge, or Wildlife where you pass a lake and a wetland preserve. Pros Other
newberry.others: Wed. Hike because of minimal elevation gain.  Did Coyote, Raven, Salal Ridge & KSS, etc.  Can do Richochet.  Bear Jammer, etc.

n-kitsap.fullDescription: This park has over 800 acres and 10 miles of trails to choose from in one of Kitsap County's largest parks, located between the towns of Kingston and Indianola.  There are many possibilities of loops and there is a variety of forest, wetlands, and the headwaters of (2) vital salmon streams:  Grovers Creek and Carpenter Creek.  The Great Peninsula Conservancy was a leading partner in conserving this area, along with the Bainbridge Island Land Trust, in addition to other agencies. Pros Other
n-kitsap.others: Can be a Wed. or Fri. hike

notch.fullDescription: Three to four routes depending upon leader's pick. Or can be done as a key exchange. Notch Pass is believed to have been a former Native American trading route for the Quilleute Tribe.  The "notch" is on  Quilcene Ridge and can sometimes be seen from the hwy.  Go by Mosquito Rock and over a couple of creeks, which are interesting! Pros Other
notch.pros: On 11/10, we did from Lower T.H. to Bark Shanty @ 8.5 mi. & 2,800'.  Rather steep first 2 mi. to Pass, down ~ 1 mi. to F.S. Rd. 27.  To Bark Shanty after ~ 1.5 mi.
notch.others: Watch for when you do it in the Fall, as it is hunting season!  Limited parking of 2-3 cars, if you do it from the Lower Quilcene T.H.  Can also park along F.S. Rd. 27.

oat.fullDescription: New route for the group that goes on the OAT from either Karpen Rd. or the Horse Trailer area.  Go about 2 miles before turning right onto an old road bed.  Go up past some mt. bike trails like Catfish Tuna, Pro-Vulture, etc.  Stay on road bed.  Go to top to the Llama trail before turning around.  Great views up the Elwha Valley & W. Herrick up towards Mt. Carrie, Fitzhenry, etc.  Come down to OAT on roadbed closer to the Living Room.  If add that one, it would be add about a mile. Pros Other
oat.pros: Saw bleeding heart; skunk cabbage; fawn lily, yellow wood violets; chocolate lilies, etc.
oat.others: Taylor Checkerspot Butterfly area near Llama trail on top.  Pass some of the mt. bike trails.

oat-eden.fullDescription: This is a portion of the OAT (Olympic Adventure Trail) off of Eden Valley Rd., as you leave in front of the parking area.  Enjoy a viewpoint at a Bench & wooden mushrooms @ ~ a mile & then proceed down a couple of switchbacks, across the flat & can go as far as the Living Room, if so desired.  Hit the truck at ~ .6 mi. before Living Room.  New bench before the Living Room! Pros Other
oat-eden.others: This is in front of the parking area to go East!  Saw hair ice once along this trail!

oat-eden-valley.fullDescription: Enjoy this 8-mile R.T. portion of the 25-mile OAT (Olympic Adventure Trail) that goes from Hwy. 112, Mile (0) to Lake Crescent. Hikers can hike on this portion of the trail from the Eden Valley Road off of Dan Kelly Rd. @ ~ M.P. 7.5 and go west for about 4 miles to ~ M.P 11.5 to the picnic table immediately after crossing Bear Creek. Pros Other
oat-eden-valley.pros: Not much views except at clearcut and one other spot where you see Striped Peak.
oat-eden-valley.others: 3.5~ mi. to clearcut.  Bev says that you can also go 3 mi. to a Bench & turn-around.  We went to Bear Creek and a picnic table beyond, which was ~ 8 mi./797'-822'. Jordi-1,243'

oat-eden-valley-east.fullDescription: This is a portion of the OAT (Olympic Adventure Trail) off of Eden Valley Rd., as you leave in front of the parking area.  Enjoy a viewpoint at a Bench & wooden mushrooms @ ~ a mile & then proceed down a couple of switchbacks, across the flat & can go as far as the Living Room, if so desired.  Hit the truck at ~ .6 mi. before Living Room.  Continue on to lower dam.  Car ride back. Pros Other

oat--joyce.fullDescription: This is off of either 101 or 112.  It's 5 miles up from the Joyce School.  Went East about 1.25 miles to Bear Creek to picnic table and then West ~ 1.5 miles past logging road to creek and old bridge with bench seat. Pros Other
oat--joyce.others: Careful during hunting season.  Logging activity?

oat--joyce-piedmont.fullDescription: We go East on the Olympic Adventure Trail (OAT) to the 2nd Bench/Picnic Table or to the Joyce Access Logging Road. Pros Other
oat--joyce-piedmont.pros: Can get muddy at the Joyce-Access logging road, so we can turn around here.

oat---mile.fullDescription: This is a popular & familiar route for many and is considered Mile “0” of the Olympic Adventure Trail off of Hwy 112. We will hike to what is called the “Living Room” with a bench and picnic table, making it a convenient turn-around spot with a nice view, as well.  An extra 1-1/2 miles can be obtained by going further to the truck and turning around. Pros Other
oat---mile.others: Can also park at the Horse Parking area, if too many cars!

oat---jp.fullDescription: This is an adventure hike introduced to us by Paul.  It is off of the Joyce-Piedmont Rd. where we park.  We head East along this trail.  There are a variety of loops here, including "Jeff's Tree Trail", Leaf Trail, and one crossing Whiskey Creek.  Can have a snack or lunch at a picnic table on the OAT Trail with nice views.  Be flexible!  Poles and waterproof boots are very helpful. Pros Other
oat---jp.others: Watch during hunting season, as hunters might be in there.  Also be careful near logging roads or avoid entirely.  Waterproof boots are helpful for crossing creek.

obstruction.fullDescription: Park on the right-hand side near the top going to Hurricane Ridge and at about 1/2 mi. before the old lodge site before the last hair-pin turn. Drop over the steep ridge ~ 100 yards to the Obstruction Point Road and then snowshoe on the relatively flat road along the ridge.   Can go by Steeple Rock @ ~ 1.5 mi. or 3.8 mi. R.T., or continuing on towards Waterhole @ ~ 3.4 mi.-3.8 mi. one way, if it is deemed to be safe and avalanche conditions are Low. Pros Other
obstruction.pros: If do summer route, it is .4 longer than winter route.  We did 5.3 mi. & 665'-915' on 2/09.  Cox Valley Trail is .67 mi. (or .25) & Steeple Rock @ ~ 1.5 or 3.4 mi. R.T.
obstruction.others: Potential avalanche area w/avalanche risk under Steeple Rock.  Experienced snowshoers on steep terrain.  We have done 5.5 mi. & 350'

obstruction-point.fullDescription: Take the Badger Valley trail to the east for a short time rounding Elk Mountain but make sure you don't descend into the valley. Instead, keep going along the ridgeline. The trail rises slowly, revealing amazing views of Mount Olympus and others to the south. Experienced drivers for this windy, narrow mountain road needed. Pros Other

odt.fullDescription: Leave from the Waterfront Park and wander to Hollywood Beach area near the Red Lion Hotel in P.A.  May see birds and river otter along this stretch on the waterfront of P.A. Regular carpool mtg time (8:15 at Sequim Safeway Gas), we will be at Hollywood Beach to watch the Polar Bear Plunge@10am Pros Other
odt.others: Do after Polar Plunge on Jan. 1st?

ozette.fullDescription: One of the most famous and popular loop hikes on the Olympic Coast. Plan for a low tide. Early start, as it will be ~ a 2-hour drive ea. way and may cost $10-15/ride. Walk the ~3-mile boardwalk, ~3.1 miles along the beach, and another 3 miles back clockwise or counter-clockwise. Wear comfortable, sturdy shoes suitable for beach walking on large rocks.  Bring poles for such and the slippery boardwalks.  Be watching for the Makah Petroglyphs at Wedding Rocks.  Do not miss! Pros Other
ozette.others: Plan on a low tide.  Chart says 5' near wedding rocks, 5.5' near window. We hiked it at 6" higher in 2024 and it was ok.

pack.fullDescription: The old Olympic Hot Springs Pack Trail was established in 1908. We will begin our hike at Herrick Road and take the West Elwha River Trail. But for this hike we’ll take the Olympic Hot Springs Pack trail located about 2.5 miles from the cars that’s just beyond a small un-bridged creek.  We turn off at the clearly evident and recently cleaned-up trail, which is marked a little way up by a wooden sign. The trail runs about 2 miles (1,125 ft. elevation gain) through a lovely forest and gradually ascends, turns, and then continues down to meet Olympic Hot Springs Road just above the Glines Canyon Dam site. We will have lunch at the Dam then we will return via the usual West Elwha route passing through the old Altair Campground. Pros Other

pats.fullDescription: Near Slab Camp.  Named for a possible meadow (prairie?) with some "native plants".  Could be an old homestead site, as well?  The mystery remains.  Cross Pat's Creek at about 1/4 mile before climbing a short way on a Jeep trail and then branching off and going on a remote, 1-1/2+-mile forested trail before coming to a DNR road.  A viewpoint of Blue Mt. about 1/4 mile up & off of the DNR road. Pros Other
pats.pros: Best to do in Spring to find native plants like Rosy Spirea; Labrador Tea, etc  Pat Willits did a field trip here under a Nesla Buckingham years' ago.
pats.others: Don't do during hunting season.  Starts of on the #2910 Rd. (at slant).  Is ~ 4.7 miles up road and 1.2 mi. from Slab Camp. 3/4 mi. down to road where you can drive in 3 mi.

peabody.fullDescription: This is a pleasant hike from the ONP Visitors' Center, which follows Peabody Creek through a ravine and over several wooden bridges up to the end at Hurricane Ridge Road. This hike offers plenty of shade on a warm day but can still be muddy in places. Bring bug repellent & trekking poles for the muddy spots! Pros Other

port.fullDescription: There are several options for this area, included trails like Secret Squirrel, Beaver Pond, and going to a viewing platform that can offer nice views of Mt. Baker and surroundings.  Access from a parking lot at the n. end of this Kitsap County Park.    Afterwards, we usually like to have lunch at the Port Gamble General Store and view the Christmas decorations and lights. Pros Other
port.others: Can do a longer hike of ~ 9.2 miles and 670' that Steve See has led and Richard S.  accessing from the s. end of the park.

pyramid.fullDescription: This hike starts from the N. Shore Picnic Area off of Camp David Jr. Rd. near Fairholme.  It goes up to a WWII enemy-airplane spotter cabin up on the precipitous summit.  At 1.5 mi., cross June Creek.  Climb steeply crossing a rather "dicey" and exposed landslide at 1.8 miles.  Use caution (and poles!) for this section.  Turn-around if need be.  At 2.7 miles, reach the ridge crest & follow an old logging road at about 3 miles.  Then, it's a final push of a 1/2 mile to the summit and cabin. Pros Other
pyramid.pros: Views of Lake Crescent and Sutherland.
pyramid.others: Do this as an Ad Hoc Hike.  Don't want to encourage some on this hike because of the "dicey" slide.  This is not for every one!

radio.fullDescription: This DNR Rd. PA-F 3100 off of Blue Mt. Rd. passes the local KSQM (91.5 FM Radio Station) bldg. We are on the road for a bit, may drop down & see Pederson & McDonald Creeks, may even walk on a loop to the irrigation ditch and might even add on a new section towards Emery Road.  Be flexible! Pros Other
radio.others: Can also go to Emery Road.  Gal we met along the ditch is Jonny Johnson!  She knows the guy who put up the sign!

robin.fullDescription: Start at Dryke Rd TH.  Come enjoy this local County Park accessible to walkers, joggers, and equestrians alike!  This park has "195 acres with 150 acres in forest management, 15 acres of open space grass fields, 5 acres of wetlands, 5 acres of plant propagation (for the ONP for transplanting native plants in the Elwha Valley), and remaining 20 acres used for agricultural farming and gardening".  There is also a section of the trail that meanders along the north property line of Pinnell Road. Pros Other

royal.fullDescription: Follow Royal Creek up to the base of a beautiful rock slide area. (There is often a waterfall seen in the late spring/early summer.)  This hike begins at Upper Dungeness Trailhead.  Pass the trail to Camp Handy on the left (crossing over Royal Creek).  Proceed on the right following Royal Creek up.  Pass the Maynard Burn Trail and hit the Natl. Park Boundary at 1.5 miles.  At the end drop down ~ 75' to Royal Creek Camp @ 3.5 mi for lunch.  Lots of Fungi. Pros Other

river.fullDescription: Go down the upper portion of the Lower Dungeness Trail, crossing a slide area to the River Shelter at about 1.75 miles; then turn-around and come back to the road and then proceed on up to Camp Handy on the Upper Dungeness Trail for ~ 3.3 mi. Pros Other
river.others: R.T. to River Shelter is 3.6 mi.  1.1 mi. to Royal Creek.  7.25 to Camp Handy R.T.

royal-lakebasin.fullDescription: This is a popular hike and backpacking destination from the Upper Dungeness.  It's a long hike.  Can get to Royal Lake at 7.2 miles after passing some camps at 6.3 miles.  Continue ~ a mile up to Upper Royal Basin and even further to the tarns. Pros Other

silver.fullDescription: Route will take hikers up the very popular Mt. Townsend Trail #839 to Camp Windy, then turn left off on the Silver Lakes Trail #842 at about 3 miles, instead of going right up towards Mt. Townsend.  Climb about 175' to Windy Gap; then descend down towards Silver Creek Valley on a couple of switchbacks.  At an unmarked intersection at ~ 4.6 miles, proceed straight ahead, climbing a bit before reaching the larger Silver Lake at ~ 5.4 miles. Pros Other
silver.pros: George added Mt. Townsend and got a total of 12.7 miles and 4,100'!  Diane got the 11 miles and 3,550'.
silver.others: Just don't do during Wilderness High Hunt of 9/15-9/25
