silver-lake.fullDescription: Quickest way to Silver Lake via the Silver Lake Way Trail near end of the Upper Dungeness Rd.  past Tubal Cain T.H.  "User-built" trail and is quite rough and rooty in a 1/2 mile section.  Hiker must be able to negotiate these big rocks in this and a couple of other steep, short sections.  Trail then has some flat meadows and moderate inclines.  Turn rt. at trail intersection to go to Silver Lake.  Also, a steep 1/2 mi. section up to saddle near Hawk's Peak w/ incredible views! Pros Other

slab.fullDescription: This is a moderately difficult to difficult hike as there are some steep grades, especially between the 1.5 – 2.7-mile mark. You can go as far as the “Benches” at 2.7 miles or to the ONP boundary at 3.3 miles or continue on to the Deer Park Campground at about 5 miles.  Or, if not enough, can go on another .8 miles to Blue Mt. and the .5 mi. Rainshadow Nature Trail! Pros Other
slab.pros: If you want to cut it short and go to the Benches, it still is a substantial climb with steep grades.  That would be about 5.5 mi. R.T. and ~ 1,660' elevation gain.

slab-camp.fullDescription: This is a moderately difficult to difficult hike as there are some steep grades, especially between the 1.5 – 2.7-mile mark. You can go as far as the “Benches” at 2.7 miles or to the ONP boundary at 3.3 miles or continue on to the Deer Park Campground at about 5 miles.  Or, if not enough, can go on another .8 miles to Blue Mt. and the .5 mi. Rainshadow Nature Trail! Pros Other
slab-camp.pros: If you want to cut it short and go to the Benches, it still is a substantial climb with steep grades.  That would be about 5.5 mi. R.T. and ~ 1,660' elevation gain.

slab-camp-to.fullDescription: This is considered a "reverse" hike as it drops down to the Upper Gray Wolf River in the Gray Wolf Valley. Cross on a sturdy bridge at the valley floor and can go up the river a bit to Camp Tony or turn around at this point. Pros Other

slab-camp-to-slide.fullDescription: This hike adds on beyond Duncan Flats and Camp Tony on the Gray Wolf River @ 6-7 mi. & 1,500-2,300'. Proceed up the Upper Gray Wolf Trail another ~ 2.8 mi. to Slide Camp, which is a campspot on Slide Creek at ~2,200' before going into the Natl. Park.  This is a Wilderness Hike from the T.H. https://connect.garmin.com/modern/activity/3464810413 Pros Other
slab-camp-to-slide.pros: Hike parallels Slide Camp towards the Gray Wolf River.

sleepy.fullDescription: This portion of the Sleepy Hollow Trail #852 (an extension) leaves from a lower parking area ~ 1 mile below the Mt. Zion T.H. parking area. This trail provides an easier alternative to the more popular Mt. Zion Trail.  One can go up to the Mt. Zion parking lot and turn-around or go towards Gold Creek, if the creek is passable & then go to Sleepy Hollow Creek! Pros Other
sleepy.others: If you add Mt. Zion from Ext. Trail, this would be ~ 11.75-12.2 mi. total & 2,163' - 2,675' & ~ 4.5 mi. R.T. (?).  Another elev. was 2,582'!  Check records.  Many possibilities here.

sleepy-hollowmt.fullDescription: Did Sleepy Hollow Trail get its name from the legend?  At a junction at ~ ¾ mi., hikers can either choose to go up ~ 3 mi. to the Mt. Zion parking lot & continue on up ~ 2.4 mi. to Mt. Zion & Viewpt.  Or, those wanting a gentler hike can go the other direction from the ¾ mi. juncture & carefully cross Gold Creek to follow the Sleepy Hollow Trail for ~ 4 miles to Sleepy Hollow Creek. Pros Other
sleepy-hollowmt.others: If you add Mt. Zion from Ext. Trail, this would be ~ 11.75-12.2 mi. total & 2,163' - 2,675' & ~ 4.5 mi. R.T. (?).  Another elev. was 2,582'!  Check records.  Many possibilities here.

smokey.fullDescription: Hikers depart from Madison Falls along the old roadbed and bypass up to Glines Canyon Dam, which is ~ 3.75 miles.  The Smokey Bottom Trail departs just west of the dam along the shoreline and in the old Lake Mills lakebed.  Spring (late May) is a good time to see some native flowers that were planted during the Elwha Revegetation Project like lupine, Nootka roses, Oregon sunshine, etc. Pros Other
smokey.pros: We hit the lupine perfectly on 5/24/2024.
smokey.others: There may be some mud & wet area when crossing Upper Stukey Creek.  Use caution on crossing on log.  The Gray Wolf crew logged it out with ~ 74 trees in 3/2024 (Lisa/Neil)

snider.fullDescription: Start at Littleton Camp for Mt. Muller.  Head up to Jim's Junction at 3 miles and 14 switchbacks gaining about 2,200'.  Turn left & go about 3/4 - 1.5 miles to a viewpoint.  Hope to have Fall colors and possibly late-season berries!  If earlier, may have some bear grass!  Can also park a car at Kloshe Nanitch and one at Muller for the 9-mile total & 2,861'. Pros Other
snider.pros: We did on 9/22.  Should've done it earlier, as no berries!  Debbie H. & I did whole Snider Ridge on 6/23/23.  Minimum of 2,084' from Littleton?

spruce.fullDescription: This is an easy walk along an old Spruce RR grade starting at East Beach road along Lake Crescent and is part of the ODT (Olympic Discovery Trail).  This was named for the spruce transported for military use during WW I.  This portion of the trail is popular for its tunnels and the picturesque Devil's Punchbowl. Pros Other

spruce-rr.fullDescription: This walk goes from the W. portion of the Spruce R.R. at Lake Crescent and heads from the N. Shore Picnic Area from the Camp David Jr. Rd. turn-off past the Fairholm Store and goes west on the Olympic Discovery Trail.  Can have a car at either end and go ~6 miles' one way to parking near Sol Duc Rd.  Options here. Pros Other
spruce-rr.others: Some times, we plan this around having a Christmas lunch at the Lake Crescent Lodge.

steam.fullDescription: Relatively easy hike from the Dosewallips State Park Campground near Brinnon. Goes through woods, over streams like Phantom Creek, and also along a trail, Steam Donkey named for equipment used in logging days. If tide permits, can go under 101 & walk out towards tidal flats & viewing from an observation tower.  If fortunate, might see spawning salmon & maybe even some elk! https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/map-c96c08f-22 Pros Other
steam.pros: Fall is best to see salmon, elk, and maybe even harbor seals!
steam.others: Some times, stop for lunch at Goeduck Tavern!  Rick says that he got about 6 miles and 600'!  I'm doubtful!  It's more like 4.7 & 563'

storm.fullDescription: Park at the Storm King Ranger Station at Lake Crescent.  Proceed towards Marymere Falls.  Storm King Trail will be on left.  From there it is a climb! Pros Other
storm.pros: Quick workout and climb up to Storm King.
storm.others: Can add the Moments of Time Trail coming back.  Discourage use of the ropes going on up.

striped.fullDescription: Many options of loops in this area, including going down to the picturesque Cove (Eagle Cove) passing Striped Peak Falls (aka Salish Maiden Falls).  Can go to the real Striped Peak @ 1,166’ (not a real peak but a high prominence), on a newly built trail in this County Park and 1500-acre DNR area.  There are also fabulous views of Crescent Bay, towards Vancouver Island across the Strait of Juan de Fuca, etc.  One might even get to see Mt. Baker! Pros Other
striped.pros: Careful during hunting season getting off the main trail on the DNR Roads on the s. side.  Stay in the County Park during this time.

striped-peak.fullDescription: Go to the Striped Peak @ 1,166’ (not a real peak but a high prominence), on a newly built trail in this County Park and 1500-acre DNR area.  There are also fabulous views of Crescent Bay, towards Vancouver Island across the Strait of Juan de Fuca, etc.  One might even get to see Mt. Baker!  https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/striped-peak Pros Other
striped-peak.pros: Careful during hunting season getting off the main trail on the DNR Roads on the s. side.  Stay in the County Park during this time.

sunrise.fullDescription: Cross below the intermediate rope tow and tubing park across from the trailer selling tickets.  Stay to the right of the ski hill & along the tree-line.  After crossing under & above the top of the rope tow, the route follows a narrow ridge toward the s. side of Mt. Angeles.  Check your avalanche conditions ahead of time for any unstable conditions, as there are cornices and avalanche prone areas along the way.  There is one steep slope after the rope tow to descend carefully. Pros Other
sunrise.others: Only do if the avalanche conditions are Low or maybe Moderate.

switchback.fullDescription: Starts at Switchback TH.  Starts at cascading stream in subalpine Alaska yellow-cedar forest and climbs 1480' in 1.6 miles, transitioning to the alpine meadows of Victor Pass with lots of wildflowers this time of year.  Continue along the ridge for a mile with continuous spectacular views (weather permitting).  Descend 400' over 0.3 miles to an outstanding raven's eye view of Lake Angeles and turnaround point.  Mostly good quality trail with scattered rocky/steep spots.  Expect a few lingering snow patches covering the trail on the East end of the ridge. If still feeling perky on the way back, can do a side trip around to the meadows on the West side of Mt. Angeles, adding 2.0 miles and 900' round trip. Pros Other

teal.fullDescription: Teal Lake Trail is 2 miles around & is in the Port Ludlow area.   Add on to this loop with a couple of other loops like Mt. Wilder Way, Olympic Terrace, DNR Connector, Niblik's Loop near Timberton Loop.  Not much viewing of the lake except from the fishing dock.  Mud & wet trails may be encountered, so bring poles. Pros Other
teal.others: May need to find another area to park, as it is a U.S. Dept. of Fish and Wildlife area and says, "Fishing Only".

timberton.fullDescription: Can start out of Port Ludlow doing the Timberton Loop and Golf 9 area at this abadoned golf course development, of which was never completed.  There are some trails around the golf course and some on old service and logging roads.  May be able to go to a beaver dam, as well.  Trail can be somewhat muddy in places.  Or, can do a route from golf course on Niblick's (named for cafe at golf course) Loop Trail (often muddy) and meander towards Teal Lake Loop.  Several options here! Pros Other
timberton.others: Can add on Port Ludlow Falls of ~ 1/2 mile and 100'.  Diane has done a lot in there and has done 7 miles and 1,142', which could be a Friday hike!

tongue.fullDescription:
Complete tour of Salt Creek Recreation Area.  Park at the Main lot by sports field, go down to salt creek, go on the beach to tongue point, then go to Eagle's Cove, then back to cars.  Possible excursion to batteries.
There are bathrooms at halfway point between batteries and Eagles cove.
very slow to rock-hop without sticks.  Friday hike can go to Striped Peak to complete the tour Pros Other

travis.fullDescription: Some cobblestone beach walk from Panorama Vista County Park on NW corner of Miller Peninsula off E. Sequim Bay Rd.  Travis Spit is across from Gibson Spit/Port Williams across WA Harbor and looking at the Battelle Pacific NW National Lab.  Views of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Protection Island, and sometimes even Mt. Baker!  Bring binoculars for bird viewing.  May see river otters and various sea creatures.  There is limited parking.  Please respect private property. Pros Other
travis.pros: May see river otters and sea creatures and birds!  Bring binoculars.  WE saw oyster catchers, killdeer, mergansers, Harlequin ducks & buffleheads?
travis.others: Check for tides.  22 steps down to beach from landing down from parking lot.  Kris got 180'?

tubal.fullDescription: Trail starts towards the end of the Upper Dungeness Rd.  Pass the Silver Creek Shelter and cross Silver Creek on a log bridge entering the Wilderness at ~ a 1/2 mile.  Hike through 2nd-growth conifers and a tunnel of rhodys.  At 3.2 mi., come to a junction.  Can go up to the left steeply less than a mi. to Tull Canyon and the plane wreckage of a WWII, B-17 bomber.  Or, can go straight up valley towards the Tubal Cain mine & the site of the old Copper City near Copper Creek. Pros Other
tubal.pros: Pacific Rhodys lining the first 3 miles.  Plane wreckage in Tull Canyon.
tubal.others: Enter Wilderness at about 1/2 mile.  Limit 12

tunnel.fullDescription: Hike is out of Quilcene going steadily up along Tunnel Creek to the Tunnel Creek Shelter @ ~3 mi. & a gain of ~ 1,300'.  Cross Tunnel Creek and start climbing up to Harrison Lake & to 5050 Pass.  There are a couple of short, technical rocky sections.  Can stop at "Lunch Rock" for its incredible view of Mt. Constance and Valhalla; or those wishing to go further, can scramble up to Valhalla--another 20 min. of ~ .3 miles and 350’-400’ where you can be looking directly at Mt. Constance. Pros Other
tunnel.pros: Views of Jupiter & The Brothers, as well.  Some stats:  ~ 2.7 to shelter & 1,100'.  Harrison is a 4.1 and 5050 at 4.7.  Valhalla another ~.3 mi.. & 400'
tunnel.others: Various stats on this.  I've had 8.7 R.T. - 9.4 & 2,574'.  It's about 2,500' to lunch rock?

tyler.fullDescription: This hike has beautiful views and has one of the steepest trails in the Olympics.  It can be brutal with one 2.1-mile section gaining 2,700'!  If you do both mts., it does add distance! Pros Other
tyler.pros: Great Views! This would made a good Ad Hoc hike.
tyler.others: For experienced hikers only.  Bring plenty of water.  Avoid during hunting season.  If you go from the lower Maynard Burn Trail, you add on another 3 mi. & ~500; elev. gain!

verne.fullDescription: Matt has offered to lead this hike along Valley Creek. We leave from his house @ 1927 S. Pine St. @ ~ 9:30 a.m. After hiking the main trail ~ 1.6 miles up to Wellman, the more adventurous will then proceed and hike an addtl. 1.7-mile extension trail towards the high school.  This portion is technically difficult and adds an  addtl. ~700’, requiring 2 creek crossings (wear waterproof boots) and use poles for the crossings and steep sections--must also be able to negotiate 18” steps.  https://www.strava.com/activities/8489751942 Pros Other

victoriacanada.fullDescription: Take the earliest Coho ferry from Port Angeles to Victoria and walk around Victoria exploring the waterfront, Beacon Hill Park, Clover Point Park, Holland Point Park, to the Breakwater Lighthouse, having lunch at the Breakwater Bistro & Bar, and returning via Fisherman's Wharf and the colorful floathouses, and Peter Pollen Park.  This will be a long day, so plan accordingly! Pros Other
victoriacanada.pros: Ferry ride from Port Angeles across the Straits of Juan de Fuca.  Sometimes river otters at the Breakwater and orcas when crossing the Straits.
victoriacanada.others: Need Passport or Enhanced Driver's License

voice.fullDescription: We will access the trails from the parking area (about 164' above sea level), near the entrance of this County Park off of Voice of America Rd.  We will walk along the bluff, view the Spit from the viewing area, down to the beach, up by the Wildlife Refuge Office, to a picnic table viewing the Olympics, through the meadow, & follow a network of other trails in this popular County Park, including seeing the largest yew tree in Clallam County! Pros Other

w.fullDescription: Park and proceed up trail respecting private property on an easement.  Campfire Girls red alder grove (1938) as you enter the Natl. Park.  Follow the west side of the Elwha across some bridges like Freeman, Deadhorse, & Hughes.   Drop down to the abandoned Altair Picnic/Campground Area.  Can proceed on up to Glines Canyon Dam on the Olympic Hot Springs Rd. Pros Other
w.pros: Wildflowers in late Spring.  Even Ghost Pipe near Hughes Bridge @ 2 miles!  Can add a 1/2 mi. going down to kayak put-in.  3.25 to Altair. 4.75 to dam.
w.others: Can be muddy in Spring.  Nice wildflowers.  Hughes Creek at ~ 1.75- 2 mi.  Can run real high in Spring.  One bridge near cliff is Deadhorse. View of Bare Btm. Beach!

waterfalls.fullDescription: Visit 4 waterfalls, which should be at their prime:  Falls View (a hiking loop near Mt. Walker), Rainbow Falls across from Mt. Walker, Rocky Brook Falls near Brinnon, a picnic lunch, & then Murhut Falls up the Duckabush. Visit Whitney Gardens in Brinnon on the way home to see the fabulous rhodies.  A $1 donation is suggested for visiting the gardens. Pros Other
waterfalls.others: Visit ~3-4 waterfalls, which should be at their prime:  Falls View (a hiking loop near Mt. Walker, Rainbow Falls across from Mt. Walker, then Rocky Brook Falls near Brinnon, perhaps a picnic lunch, & then Murhut Falls up the Duckabush, if time allows.  Bonus options are seeing the High Steel Bridge or visiting Whitney Gardens in Brinnon to see the fabulous rhodies.  A $1 donation is suggested for visiting the gardens!  Choose your carpool accordingly.

wolf.fullDescription: Snowshoe from Hurricane Ridge parking to the Wolf Creek Trail.  Go down the fairly steep slope near the 1st set of restrooms to avoid any possible avalanche potential and stay along the treeline.  Drop down to the summer trail and head down to a Lunch spot view point or just beyond the "Sno-Tel" site. Pros Other
wolf.pros: New workout for the group! ~ .6 mi. from parking lot to the trail or a bit further.  ~ 1.55 mi. to "Sno-Tel" site at one corner before it heads southeast (?) Yellow sign in tree.
wolf.others: Reverse Hike so it's quite a workout coming back up!  Did w/ the Ramblers and then OTHH on 3/22/24

wolf-creek.fullDescription: Hike starts up at Hurricane Ridge going down the Wolf Creek Trail, which is the old road up to Hurricane Ridge!  Get view of the Olympics and follow this old road bed, as it heads down 8 miles to the end of the Whiskey Bend Road and T.H.  Follow Whiskey Bend Rd. to the Elwha Ranger Station and out to Madison Falls parking. Pros Other
wolf-creek.others: Need a car shuttle.  I did it on July 4th & enjoyed it for the wildflowers!

whidbey.fullDescription: We walk from the ferry terminal through some of Camp Casey's/Fort Ebey's trail system and go through some of the Admiralty Inlet Natural Area Preserve. Pros Other
whidbey.pros: Hope to see some of the blooming Common Camas and Golden Paintbrush.
whidbey.others: Go in earlier May or late April (?)  We were a little late last time.

wolf-creek---12.fullDescription: Hike down Wolf Creek Trail, which is ~ .6 mi. from Hurricane Ridge.  This is a reverse hike.  Quite pleasant on this old roadway!  Wildflowers abundant in late June/early July.  Go about 1.5 mi. to snow telematary site on corner (marked with yellow triangular marker).  Proceed on old roadway past 2 viewpoints.  Good turn-around point is at about 3.6-3.8 miles at S.E. side (looks down towards Elwha River).  Wolf Creek Trail does proceed on down to Whiskey Bend Rd. @ ~ 8 miles. Pros Other
wolf-creek---12.pros: No people!  They are all doing Hurricane Hill!
